name: DC-DC Fast Charge Module 6~32V to 5V/3A (DFRobot DFR0756)
//: Catalog draft written by /spark:research on 2026-09-29 while researching the irrigation controller's 12 V -> 5 V buck; not chosen (see //why_not). Facts come ONLY from the DFRobot text at the cited URLs; photo and PDF URLs are listed in sources so `parts.py --fetch` keeps them, and were not read. verified:true = the vendor's own text at the URL; nothing here was measured or inferred. No wiki page is linked from the product page. The product page also lists sibling variants (10.5~32V to 5V3A $6.50, 2-way $5.90, 4-way $7.90) under other SKUs not recorded here.
//why_not: A USB fast-charge module: its output is a USB socket that negotiates 3-12 V with whatever plugs in, which is the opposite of a fixed 5 V rail for a carrier board.
//sources: The photo file names on DFRobot's CDN contain spaces and parentheses; they are cited percent-encoded so a fetch can resolve them.
//pins: Output is a USB socket ('USB output', Features); the input connector is not described in text.

body_mm.why_it_matters: not stated on the product page; no wiki page found ('Small in size' is all it says)

output_volts_default.why_it_matters: product page: 'Output Voltage: 3-12V Auto-adjust based on the fast-charging protocol (Default output 5V, the input should be 2V higher than the output)' — the rail moves if the load negotiates.

input_headroom_v.why_it_matters: 'the input should be 2V higher than the output'

protections.value: input overvoltage, under-voltage, input overcurrent, output overcurrent, short circuit, over-temperature
protections.why_it_matters: product page 'Chip Protection' line, verbatim list

fast_charge_protocols.value: DCP, BC1.2, Apple, Samsung, Huawei FCP/SCP, Spreadtrum SFCP, Qualcomm QC2.0/3.0, MTK PE1.1/PE2.0
fast_charge_protocols.why_it_matters: product page 'Supported Fast Charging Protocol' — the reason its output voltage is not fixed.

sourcing.note: structured data price 2.9; schema.org InStock on the day
